title: Extraction of DNA from Blood Samples Using Flexigene Kit
author: Eyleen Nabyla Alvarenga Niitsuma
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.se4ebgw
materials: Pipet 5 ml Buffer FG1 into a 10 ml centrifuge tube. Add 2 ml whole blood and mix by inverting the tube 5 times. undetermined, whole blood sample undetermined, Buffer FG1 Buffer FG1 (lysis buffer) Qiagen Catalog #51206

steps.title: Initial centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 5 min at 2000 × g in a swing‑out rotor.

steps.title: Protein digestion incubation
steps.instruction: Invert the tube 3 times, place it in a heating block or water bath, and incubate at 65 °C for 10 min. The sample should change color from red to olive‑green, indicating protein digestion.

steps.title: Add denaturation buffer and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml Buffer FG2 (Qiagen catalog #51206) containing Protease, close the tube, and vortex immediately with 3–4 high‑speed pulses of ~5 s each until the pellet is completely homogenized. Inspect the tube; if any jelly‑like pellet remnants remain, add an additional 300 µl Buffer FG2 and vortex again.

steps.title: Remove supernatant and invert
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant and leave the tube inverted on a clean sheet of absorbent paper for 2 min, taking care that the pellet remains in the tube. If the pellet is loose, pour the supernatant slowly.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml 100 % isopropanol and mix thoroughly by inversion until the DNA precipitate becomes visible as threads or a clump. For samples with very low white‑blood‑cell counts, invert the tube at least 20 times.

steps.title: Pellet DNA by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 3 min at 2000 × g. If the resulting pellet is loose, prolong the spin or increase the g‑force.

steps.title: Remove isopropanol supernatant
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant and briefly invert the tube onto a clean piece of absorbent paper, ensuring the pellet stays in the tube. A visible white pellet should be present if the white‑blood‑cell count was sufficient.

steps.title: Wash pellet with ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml 70 % ethanol and vortex for 5 s.

steps.title: Second ethanol centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 3 min at 2000 × g. If the pellet is loose, prolong the spin or increase the g‑force.

steps.title: Remove ethanol and invert drying
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant and leave the tube inverted on a clean piece of absorbent paper for at least 5 min, taking care that the pellet remains in the tube. Pour slowly if the pellet is loose.

steps.title: Air‑dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the DNA pellet until all liquid has evaporated (minimum 5 min). Avoid over‑drying, which makes the DNA difficult to dissolve.

steps.title: Rehydrate DNA in Buffer FG3
steps.instruction: Add 200 µl Buffer FG3 (Qiagen catalog #51206), vortex for 5 s at low speed, and incubate for 1 h at 65 °C in a heating block or water bath to dissolve the DNA. If DNA is not fully dissolved, incubate overnight at room temperature. If a reduced volume of Buffer FG3 is used, extend the incubation time accordingly.
